---
title: "Common withholding cost and matched disclosure"
subtitle: "3.8 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 22–23"
description: "Risk comparisons at a common cost and error comparisons at a common disclosure level."
---

Rules that disclose different numbers of pairs can be compared two ways: by total risk at a common withholding price τ, or by expected wrong directions at matched disclosure N under one posterior.

```{=html}

```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Same τ, .20.** Posterior-mean tiers state 21 pairs with risk .161, while the best report states 17 pairs with risk .146.
- **Same N, eight units.** At matched disclosure N 21, posterior-mean tiers leave excess-error gap .163 above H(21).
- **Thirty units, one order.** Among 436 three-grade cuts, posterior-mean tiers state 300 pairs with E 48.3 on the order boundary.
- **Thirty units, same τ.** Without the grade cap, the order family spans 536,870,912 contiguous cuts of the posterior-mean order.
- **Flags outside the order.** Evidence flags lie outside this family: risk is still evaluated, without an order-family benchmark.
- **All-withheld.** Disclosing 0 pairs gives risk .200 at τ .20, with undefined wrong share among stated pairs.

<details>
<summary>Scope and posterior notes</summary>

We evaluate the rules under the same normal posterior. The flags use the mean of all thirty estimates as their
reference. For thirty units, the boundary comes from the hull of contiguous cuts in the given order. The
withholding cost determines the loss, and the report family determines which benchmarks are available. An
allocation or classification decision would require its own objective.

</details>

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In postrank"}

The package's synthetic `pr_example_gaussian` poverty example uses its own thirty sites. At τ .25 with at most four
grades, this prints quantile cuts with N 337 and risk .1758, versus optimal cuts with N 303 and risk .1603. The risks correspond to different N; H(m) is not a package output.

```r
library(postrank)
w <- c(poverty=1, frl=0, snap=0); s <- postrank_settings(weights=w, tau=.25, G_max=4L); sc <- pr_example_gaussian$means[, "poverty"]
sapply(c("quantile", "optimal"), function(r) unlist(postrank_cuts(sc, pr_example_gaussian, s, direction="descending", rule=r)$evaluation[c("N", "primary_risk")]))
```

:::
